events.title: EyesOpenCTF 7th edition
events.description:
EyesOpenCTF 2026 is a FREE CTF competition organized as part of the 7th edition of EOCON.

This year, the competition goes far beyond a traditional CTF.
You are not simply joining to solve isolated challenges. You are entering The Convergence, a live 48-hour cyber adventure in which reality itself is beginning to fracture.
Across more than 40 challenges and 8 disciplines, teams will investigate corrupted systems, recover hidden Reality Fragments, unlock classified dossiers, expose compromised actors, and gradually reconstruct the truth behind a phenomenon threatening the entire world.

Every flag matters.
Each solved challenge can reveal new intelligence, unlock characters and locations, alter the mission briefing, and move the story forward in real time. The competition platform becomes a living investigation that evolves with the progress of the Operators.

Expect  : 
- web exploitation, 
- digital forensics, 
- reverse engineering, 
- binary exploitation, 
- cryptography, 
- OSINT, 
- AI security, and more—woven into a single coherent mission unlike any previous EyesOpenCTF.

Built for teams from around the world and open to different experience levels, EyesOpenCTF is both a proving ground and an immersive narrative experience where competitors can learn, compete, get noticed, and join a fast-growing international cybersecurity community.

As part of EOCON, the competition also connects participants with experts, researchers, recruiters, entrepreneurs, and emerging talent from Africa and beyond. It is a place where technical ability meets storytelling, where discoveries change the mission, and where tomorrow’s collaborations, careers, and opportunities begin.

Form your team. Enter the Protocol. Recover the Fragments.

Register: https://eyesopensecurity.com/ctf-briefing.html

Direct Form: https://eyesopensecurity.com/?modal=ctf

SPONSORS :
- CyberDefenders (https://cyberdefenders.org)
- JetBrains (https://jetbrains.com)
- Netticket (https://netticket.net)
- ExamBoot (https://examboot.net)

Format:
- Modified jeopardy style. Realistic IT environment.
- Regional qualifiers are held in Nov-Dec each year.
- National finals are the following July.
- Winning teams represent Canada at international events in the Fall.

For nationals:
Participants will be the winning team from each regional/qualifier

- AND one all-women team (chosen from participants at the Regionals).
Two-day event.

events.title: Leo's 20th Birthday Bash
events.description:
Hey! You there! Do you like programming? Do you like puzzles? Do you like... money?

Leo's 20th Birthday Bash is a 24-hour online team contest that's competitive-programming-ish, CTF-ish, math-olympiad-ish, and puzzle-hunt-ish, all wrapped into one.

The contest runs on DMOJ, an online judge for competitive programming, and each team shares one DMOJ account to submit from. Teams can have 1 to 10 members (6 to 8 recommended).

Some problems are CTF-ish, but DMOJ itself is not part of the contest, so please do not attack, probe, or abuse it. The people at DMOJ are hosting this for free >.<

This contest has no sponsors, so all the prize money is from yours truly ;)

Make sure you've read all the rules (see the contest page). In particular, interactive generative AI is not allowed, because it is stinky.

See you there!

events.title: THE FINAL EXPLOIT CTF 2026—QUALIFIERS
events.description:
THE FINAL EXPLOIT CTF 2026 — QUALIFIERS

ONE LAST FLAG. ONE FINAL EXPLOIT.

The year is coming to an end, but there's one last challenge waiting.

Organized by 0xV01D, THE FINAL EXPLOIT CTF 2026 is a 48-hour international online Jeopardy-style competition, open to CTF teams worldwide.

Compete against teams from around the world, solve challenging cybersecurity problems, demonstrate your real-world skills, and earn your place in THE FINAL EXPLOIT CTF 2026 — GRAND FINAL.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

EVENT DETAILS

Dates: December 29–31, 2026
Start: December 29 at 12:00 UTC
End: December 31 at 12:00 UTC
Duration: 48 hours
Format: Online | Jeopardy-style
Participation: Team-based | Worldwide
Organizer: 0xV01D
Prizes: To be announced

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

CHALLENGE CATEGORIES

• Web Exploitation
• Binary Exploitation (Pwn)
• Reverse Engineering
• Cryptography
• OSINT
• Digital Forensics & Incident Response (DFIR)
• Malware Analysis
• Mobile Security
• AI Security
• Blockchain Security
• Miscellaneous

BEYOND TRADITIONAL CTF CHALLENGES

This competition goes beyond conventional CTF puzzles.

Participants will face realistic, industry-inspired cybersecurity scenarios designed to test practical skills used by security professionals in real-world environments.

Expect hands-on challenges involving:

• Security Operations Center (SOC) investigations and threat detection
• Real-world penetration testing methodologies and exploitation scenarios
• Digital forensics and incident response investigations
• Analysis of authentic or realistically simulated security logs, network traffic, and system artifacts
• Threat hunting, attack reconstruction, and incident analysis
• Practical security challenges inspired by real operational environments

These challenges are designed to bridge the gap between CTF competitions and the cybersecurity industry, encouraging participants to develop job-relevant skills in offensive and defensive security.

NOT JUST FLAGS. REAL SKILLS. REAL-WORLD SECURITY.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

THE ROAD TO THE GRAND FINAL

50 TEAMS. ONE GRAND FINAL. ONE CHAMPION.

The top 50 eligible teams will qualify for THE FINAL EXPLOIT CTF 2026 — GRAND FINAL through four main divisions.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

01 | INTERNATIONAL DIVISION — 20 SLOTS

The International Division is divided into two categories:

A. INTERNATIONAL OPEN — 16 SLOTS

The 16 highest-scoring eligible international teams will qualify.

This category is open to male, mixed-gender

B. INTERNATIONAL WOMEN — 4 SLOTS

The 4 highest-scoring eligible international all-women teams will qualify.

Teams must consist entirely of female participants.

Qualification is based on the official competition scoreboard and final scores.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

02 | JORDANIAN UNIVERSITY DIVISION — 10 SLOTS

The 10 highest-scoring eligible teams representing universities in Jordan will qualify.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

03 | JORDANIAN SCHOOL DIVISION — 10 SLOTS

The 10 highest-scoring eligible teams representing schools in Jordan will qualify.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

04 | JORDANIAN WOMEN'S DIVISION — 10 SLOTS

The 10 highest-scoring eligible all-women teams from Jordan will qualify.

REQUIREMENTS:

• Every team member must be female.
• Teams must represent Jordan.
• Teams may include students from different schools and universities.
• Mixed educational backgrounds are fully permitted, including teams combining school and university students.
• Qualification is based on the final competition scores.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

QUALIFICATION RULES

• The qualifiers are open to teams worldwide.
• A total of 50 teams will advance to the Grand Final.
• All rankings are determined by the official competition scoreboard.
• Each team may claim only one Grand Final qualification slot.
• If a team qualifies in multiple divisions, its qualification slot will be assigned according to the official eligibility rules, and the next highest-scoring eligible team will advance.
• Full eligibility requirements, team verification procedures, and Grand Final rules will be published on the official event website.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

OFFICIAL INFORMATION

Website: https://0xv01d-ctf.xyz/

Further details regarding the Grand Final, team eligibility, competition rules, and prizes will be announced on our official website.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

See you on the scoreboard.

events.title: JerseyCTF VII
events.description:
Locations:
- Online if unable to attend in-person
- In-Person @ NJIT Campus Center Ballroom, Newark, New Jersey

JerseyCTF is a beginner-friendly Capture the Flag competition that aims to inspire interest in cybersecurity. This competition is hosted by the NJIT Information & Cybersecurity Club, the NJIT Chapter of ACM, and the NJIT SCI program.

It is geared towards students, beginners, and professionals alike. JerseyCTF provides participants with jeopardy-style questions in categories including cryptography, forensics, binary exploitation/reversing, open-source intelligence, and web exploitation.

This CTF is held hybrid - with attendance virtually or in-person on NJIT's campus in Newark, New Jersey, USA.
